cases.input: Analyze a core antibody patent family deeply. Extract VH/VL and CDR-linked sequence disclosures, claimed functional binding definitions, epitope evidence, KD/competition data, assay examples and reconstruct the disclosed technical embodiment.
requiredBehaviors: separate claimed features from disclosed embodiments and experimentally demonstrated data
map sequence IDs to antibody domains and claim or example references
retain assay method and measurement context for binding data
produce a reconstruction baseline using only publicly supported details
forbiddenBehaviors: treat a competition-binding claim as proof of an exact residue epitope
invent missing CDRs sequences affinities or assay conditions

cases.input: A biotechnology patent contains an ST.26 XML sequence listing with many SEQ IDs plus several sequences repeated under different identifiers across continuation members.
requiredBehaviors: prefer the machine-readable sequence listing over manual extraction from narrative PDF text
normalize type length sequence provenance and patent-internal identifiers
use a stable sequence checksum to identify identical sequences across IDs or members
preserve sequence-to-claim and sequence-to-example relationships
forbiddenBehaviors: collapse sequence identifiers without retaining provenance
assume every sequence in the listing is claim-limiting

cases.input: The patent reports KD values measured by SPR, IC50 values from a competition assay and endpoint signal ratios from ELISA for several binders. Conditions are only partly reported.
requiredBehaviors: store each result with parameter unit method molecule identity and source
record missing temperature buffer immobilization or sample context where applicable
warn that results from different assay methods are not automatically directly comparable
forbiddenBehaviors: rank binders solely by numeric magnitude across incompatible assay methods
skillAnchors: nicht ohne Kontext als direkt vergleichbar

cases.input: An independent claim broadly defines a binder by target and functional activity, while the examples only demonstrate two concrete antibodies with specific sequences.
requiredBehaviors: represent the broad functional claim separately from the two demonstrated species
identify genus-versus-species and functional-versus-structural scope drivers
avoid treating experimental support for two species as proof that all claimed functional variants were demonstrated
forbiddenBehaviors: equate claimed genus with experimentally tested embodiments
describe every functionally claimed binder as a disclosed concrete sequence

cases.input: A diagnostic patent discloses the capture and detection antibody sequences and the detection chemistry, but not reagent concentrations, incubation times or several calibration details.
requiredBehaviors: reconstruct the supported architecture and known reagent identities
classify missing process parameters as explicit evidence gaps
grade reconstructability as medium or low depending on criticality of missing parameters
forbiddenBehaviors: claim that the assay has been fully reproduced from the patent

cases.input: A PCT application contains broad sequence-identity claims, a later US continuation narrows to a competition-binding antibody class, and an EP divisional grants with a specific CDR combination.
requiredBehaviors: preserve the common family context while analyzing materially distinct claim-scope branches
compare jurisdiction- and member-specific claim limitations and prosecution changes
route any concrete product read-on assessment to freedom-to-operate-assessment
forbiddenBehaviors: present the family as having one uniform protection scope
make a final infringement or FTO conclusion

cases.input: After analyzing the claims and embodiments, propose technical directions for avoiding claim-critical features while preserving the diagnostic function.
requiredBehaviors: distinguish claim-critical performance-critical example-specific interchangeable and unknown features
present alternative technical directions as hypotheses rather than patent-clearance conclusions
require a new product-specific FTO screen before relying on a changed configuration
forbiddenBehaviors: state that a proposed change is patent free
generate unsupported new biological sequences as though they came from the patent
